scholarships.title: Lee Kong Chian Scholars' Programme (LKCSP)
scholarships.funding_label: Full Tuition Fee Waiver + Living Allowance

existing.description: The Lee Kong Chian Scholars' Programme is one of Singapore Management University's most prestigious undergraduate scholarships, made possible by a gift from the Lee Foundation, with up to 60 scholarships funded. It is open to full-time SMU first-year undergraduates of any nationality taking a single or double degree programme, and requires a second major or an equivalent breadth requirement, demonstrated leadership and communications skills, and a substantial record of co-curricular activity or community service. Benefits comprise a waiver of annual subsidised tuition fees for regular terms for up to four years, a S$16,000 Global Opportunities grant funding overseas exchange, community service or competitions, a S$5,000 annual living allowance, a S$1,800 one-time computer allowance, and development opportunities from SMU's Student Success Centre. Applicants are considered through the Scholarship section of the standard admission application, with no separate scholarship form. The scholarship is bond-free, but non-Singaporean scholars must sign a Ministry of Education Tuition Grant agreement obliging them to work for Singapore-based companies for three years after graduation.
eligibility: Full-time SMU first year undergraduate student of any nationality
Option of enrolling in a single degree or double degree programme

Scholars enrolled into a single degree programme other than the Bachelor of Integrative Studies must take a second major: if the primary degree is the Bachelor of Business Management, a second major offered by another SMU School; if the primary degree is in Accountancy, Economics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Computing & Law, Software Engineering, Social Sciences or Law, a second major offered by the SMU Lee Kong Chian School of Business

Scholars enrolled into the Bachelor of Integrative Studies as a single degree programme must take a second major offered by the SMU Lee Kong Chian School of Business, or include at least 6 Course Units offered by that School within their Individualised Major

Scholars enrolled into a double degree programme must pursue the Bachelor of Business Management, or the Bachelor of Integrative Studies with an Individualised Major including at least 6 Course Units offered by the SMU Lee Kong Chian School of Business
Substantial record of co-curricular activity and/or community service involvement
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to full-time SMU first-year undergraduate students of any nationality, with the option of enrolling in a single degree or a double degree programme. Scholars must take a second major (or, for the Bachelor of Integrative Studies, meet an equivalent requirement), must demonstrate leadership and communications skills, and must have a substantial record of co-curricular activity and/or community service involvement.
benefits: Waiver of annual subsidised tuition fees for regular terms (semesters 1 and 2) for up to four years
S$1,800 one-time computer allowance upon enrolment
Participation in development opportunities offered by the Student Success Centre
coverage: Waiver of annual subsidised tuition fees for regular terms (semesters 1 and 2), for up to four years

S$16,000 Global Opportunities grant funding part or a combination of an overseas student exchange or summer programme, an overseas community service project, and overseas case competitions and conference presentations
S$1,800 one-time computer allowance upon enrolment
Participation in development opportunities offered by the Student Success Centre
requirements: Indicate interest in the Scholarship section of the online admission application form
Submit the scholarship personal essay online with the admission application
Non-Singaporean scholars are required to apply for and take up the tuition grant provided by the Singapore Government, signing a Tuition Grant agreement with the Ministry of Education
documents: SMU undergraduate admission application form, indicating interest in the Scholarship section
Scholarship personal essay, completed and submitted online when applying for admission
Recommendation letters by tutor or principal (optional but strongly encouraged)
application_method: Apply for admission to SMU through the online undergraduate application form
Indicate interest in the scholarship in the Scholarship section of that application form - there is no separate scholarship application form
Complete and submit the scholarship personal essay online as part of the admission application

Optionally nominate a tutor or principal as referee using the nomination details provided in the Scholarship section of the online admission application, allowing the referee sufficient time to submit the recommendation online
existing.selection_notes: Applicants will be shortlisted based on their academic qualifications and the strength of their non-academic records. SMU's dedicated Student Success Centre implements and oversees development programmes for LKCSP scholars and is committed to guiding and developing their intellectual and holistic growth. Up to 60 scholarships are funded.
existing.best_fit: Exceptional school-leavers of any nationality applying to SMU as a first-year undergraduate who can commit to a second major or double degree, have a strong co-curricular and community service record, and are willing to accept the three-year Tuition Grant work obligation that applies to all non-Singaporean scholars.
existing.notes: The official page states: "This scholarship is bond-free. However, non-Singaporean students (including Singapore Permanent Residents) are required to sign a Tuition Grant agreement with the Ministry of Education and will be contractually obliged to work for Singapore-based companies for 3 years upon graduation from SMU." SMU's international-students listing summarises the same award slightly differently, referring to "a full four-year tuition fee waiver, a one-off notebook grant, sponsorship for an international exchange programme, an overseas study mission, and an international community service project"; the dedicated LKCSP page figures are used here as the authoritative statement.
existing.duration: Waiver of annual subsidised tuition fees for regular terms (semesters 1 and 2) for up to four years, alongside an annual living allowance.
existing.application_period: Considered automatically through the SMU undergraduate admission application for the August intake. For the last published cycle, Academic Year 2026-27, applications opened 17 November 2025 and closed 19 March 2026, with interviews notified January to July 2026 and classes starting 17 August 2026. The Academic Year 2027-28 opening and closing dates were not yet published as at 2026-10-04.
existing.deadline_display: There is no separate scholarship application or scholarship deadline: the official page states "please indicate your interest in the Scholarship section of the online application form for admission. There is no separate scholarship application form." The scholarship therefore follows the SMU undergraduate admission closing date. The official SMU 'Important Dates' page last published "Application Opening Date 17 November 2025 12.00pm, Singapore Standard Time" and "Application Closing Date 19 March 2026 11.59pm, Singapore Standard Time" for Academic Year 2026-27; dates for the next intake were not published as at 2026-10-04.
existing.program_type: Distinguished merit-based undergraduate scholarship for freshmen, donor-funded by the Lee Foundation

scholarships.title: SUTD PhD President's Graduate Fellowship (PGF)
scholarships.official_source: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)

existing.description: The SUTD PhD President's Graduate Fellowship is awarded by the Singapore University of Technology and Design to PhD candidates of all nationalities. It covers the applicable tuition fees for up to four years and pays a monthly stipend, with rates effective from 1 January 2026 of S$5,300 for Singapore Citizens, S$4,800 for Singapore Permanent Residents and S$4,300 for international students. Singapore Citizens additionally receive CPF contributions at the prevailing employer's contribution rate on top of the stipend. Students must perform teaching or laboratory supervision duties in order to fulfil the requirements for the subsidised fees.
eligibility: PhD candidates at the Singapore University of Technology and Design
Students must perform teaching / laboratory supervision duties to fulfil the requirements for the subsidised fees
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to all nationalities. The Fellowship is for candidates reading a PhD at SUTD. All holders must perform teaching or laboratory supervision duties in order to fulfil the requirements for the subsidised fees.
benefits: Applicable tuition fees covered for up to 4 years
Monthly stipend: S$5,300 Singapore Citizen, S$4,800 Singapore Permanent Resident, S$4,300 International Student (with effect from 1 January 2026)
CPF contributions at a rate pegged to the prevailing employer's contribution rate set by CPF, on top of the monthly stipend, for Singapore Citizens
coverage: Applicable tuition fees for up to 4 years
Monthly stipend of S$4,300 (international student), S$4,800 (Singapore Permanent Resident) or S$5,300 (Singapore Citizen), with effect from 1 January 2026
CPF contributions at the prevailing employer's contribution rate on top of the monthly stipend for Singapore Citizens
requirements: Perform teaching or laboratory supervision duties to fulfil the requirements for the subsidised fees
documents: SUTD PhD admission application submitted through admission.sutd.edu.sg
application_method: Apply to a SUTD PhD programme through SUTD's admission portal
Be admitted to the PhD programme; the Fellowship is awarded to awardees and has no separate application form
existing.selection_notes: The official page states the scholarships listed are tenable for graduate studies at SUTD and that the PGF is open to all nationalities. No further selection criteria, weighting or shortlisting process is published on the scholarship page.
existing.best_fit: PhD candidates of any nationality admitted to SUTD who need full tuition coverage plus a monthly stipend and are able to take on teaching or laboratory supervision duties.
existing.notes: Stipend figures shown are the international-student rate because this row targets international applicants. Important distinction: the additional stipend of up to S$500 per month after passing the PhD Qualifying Examination is stated on the official page only for the separate SUTD PhD Fellowship (footnote 3), not for the President's Graduate Fellowship, so it is not claimed here. No book, travel, computer or thesis allowance is listed for the PGF.
existing.duration: The scholarship covers the applicable tuition fees for up to 4 years.
existing.application_period: The Fellowship has no separate application; it is awarded to candidates admitted to a PhD programme at SUTD, and applications are submitted through SUTD's admission portal at https://admission.sutd.edu.sg/. Closing dates are set per programme and per intake.
existing.deadline_display: The official scholarship page states no application deadline: it lists only the award terms and stipend rates. SUTD publishes application closing dates per programme and per intake on its graduate admissions pages, for example "Application closes 31 Dec 2026 (2027 intake)" for the Master of Architecture and "31 May 2027 (September 2027 intake)" for the September 2027 MSc intakes, so the closing date for a PhD applicant follows the specific programme and intake.
